name: Hophni
overview: Hophni was a male member of the tribe of Levi and is notably identified as the son of Eli, a corrupt priest. His role and character are primarily understood in relation to his father and his priestly lineage. Scripture highlights his connection to a priestly family marked by moral failure.
namesAndTitles: The name Hophni means "tadpole" in Hebrew, as recorded in 1 Samuel 1:3. This is his proper name and was not given by God. No additional titles or meanings are associated with his name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Hophni is explicitly identified as the son of Eli, as stated in 1 Samuel 1:3. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further details about his family relationships beyond his connection to Eli.
scriptureSignificance: Hophni's significance in the biblical narrative is closely tied to his father Eli, who served as a priest but was corrupt. This association places Hophni within a priestly context marked by failure and moral compromise, which serves as a backdrop for understanding the spiritual state of Israel during that time.
